SRC-019:R4.evidence: audit_enqueue.py: new _digest_match_layer (audit_enqueue.py:462) plus an ABSENT-only recovery branch in enqueue (audit_enqueue.py:527). The allocator is the only home of producer+producer_operation_id -> layer, so when it is missing the surviving bytes are the evidence: a layer already carrying exactly this digest (on disk, or recorded in the audit inbox binding after the file was consumed) IS this operation's delivery, so the operation record is rebuilt onto that layer instead of a second layer being spent. DEVIATION from the receipt's prescribed remedy: the receipt asked for ABSENT-over-history to fail closed. Implemented and then reverted, because refusing there contradicts two shipped guarantees that have tests -- Allocation.test_manual_high_drop_advances_the_allocator_and_is_not_overwritten and Allocation.test_a_number_consumed_before_this_allocator_existed_is_never_reissued, both of which enqueue into a project that HAS layer history and NO allocator. Byte identity fixes the reproduced defect without refusing those two legitimate paths; the cost is that two distinct operations sending identical bytes collapse into one delivery, and only while the allocator is missing. With a readable allocator the operation map stays authoritative.
